examples.label: Disassemble main to find the connect call
RDX holds the plaintext DB connection string at the breakpoint
Inspect a bundled .NET DLL for more secrets

notes: Break on the driver connect call (SQLDriverConnect) and read RDX to grab the plaintext DB connection string a compiled client hides. Set intel flavor first so the disassembly is readable.
name: Apps Connecting to Services - Extract Credentials via gdb
command:
gdb ./<binary>
b *<SQLDriverConnect_addr>
run   # then inspect RDX for the connection string
description: For a compiled client that connects to a DB, breakpoint on the connect call (e.g. SQLDriverConnect) and read the registers to recover the plaintext connection string (SERVER/UID/PWD). .NET DLLs can be read with dnSpy.

defense.why_it_works: Thick client applications construct database connection strings at runtime, often assembling from encrypted components before passing to the database driver. A GDB breakpoint at SQLDriverConnect captures the fully assembled plaintext connection string from CPU registers before use.
defense.prerequisites: Access to the thick client binary. Ability to run GDB on the host. Application process is debuggable (no anti-debug protection).
defense.impact: Extraction of database credentials enabling direct database access and full data exfiltration, bypassing all application-layer access controls.
defense.detection: GDB process attached to the application (ptrace syscall). Debugger listed in process table as parent of application. Auditd log: ptrace on application PID.
defense.artifacts: Auditd log: ptrace syscall on application PID | Process table: gdb parent of application | Linux audit: PTRACE_ATTACH on protected process
defense.prevention: Enable prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 0) to prevent ptrace attachment. Store credentials in OS keychain. Use a backend API that authenticates clients with tokens -- never expose DB credentials to the client.
defense.misconfiguration: Application holds DB connection string with plaintext credentials in process memory. Application is debuggable (default) with no ptrace protection.
defense.vulnerable_config:
# Process memory contains:
DRIVER={ODBC Driver 17}; SERVER=localhost,1401; UID=app_user; PWD=P@ssw0rd!
# prctl(PR_SET_DUMPABLE, 1)  # default -- allows debugging
